shared_elements: incised/carved linear geometric motifs on a flat stone face
a lattice or grid-like arrangement of straight lines
rows of small repeated linear marks
justification: Both surfaces bear schematic, purely linear incised motifs — A a lattice/net pattern over a pillar face with a low-relief quadruped beneath, B a rectilinear framed field with rows of stick-like signs and a large arc-and-shaft figure — so the only real correspondence is the generic use of straight-line geometric patterning and small repeated strokes. The decisive differences are that A depicts an animal in relief with an all-over net pattern and no ordered framing, while B is organised as bordered bands of sign-like marks enclosing a single central curved-and-straight composition, with no creature of any kind.
